player_action: I rolled a natural 20 on my Climb check, so I automatically succeed, right?
game_state: Climb DC 25 wall, character's Climb modifier +2.
correct_ruling: No. A natural 20 is not an automatic success on a skill check (that rule applies to attack rolls and saving throws). The total is 22, which fails DC 25.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 SkillsI.rtf > Skill Checks (no automatic success on skill checks)
common_wrong_rulings: Natural 20 is a 'critical success' with bonus effects

player_action: I rolled a 1 on my Jump check. Do I automatically fail?
game_state: Jump modifier +15, DC 10 gap.
correct_ruling: No. Skill checks have no automatic failure on a natural 1; the total of 16 beats DC 10 and the jump succeeds.

player_action: I take 10 on my Climb check while the ogre is swinging at me.
game_state: Character is in melee, threatened by an ogre, climbing a rope.
correct_ruling: Not allowed. You can take 10 only when not being threatened or distracted; being in melee with an ogre prevents it. Roll the check.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 SkillsI.rtf > Checks without Rolls > Taking 10
common_wrong_rulings: Climb specifically allows take 10 in combat (it does not by default)

player_action: I take 20 to disable the trap on the chest.
game_state: Rogue with Disable Device; the trap triggers if the check fails by 5 or more.
correct_ruling: Not allowed. Taking 20 assumes you fail many times before succeeding, so it can't be used when failure carries a penalty — failing Disable Device by 5+ springs the trap.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 SkillsI.rtf > Taking 20; SkillsI/II > Disable Device
common_wrong_rulings: Allowing take 20 because there's no combat
Allowing take 20 but at x10 time

player_action: I take 20 to Search the room. How long does it take?
game_state: Searching a 5x5 ft area normally takes a full-round action.
correct_ruling: Taking 20 takes 20 times as long as a single check: 20 full rounds (2 minutes) for that 5-foot square.

player_action: I help the rogue search the room. What does that give her?
game_state: Both characters in the room; rogue making a Search check.
correct_ruling: Aid another: you make a Search check against DC 10; on success the rogue gets a +2 bonus on her check.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 SkillsI.rtf > Combining Skill Attempts > Aid Another

player_action: I have 5 ranks in Tumble. Doesn't that help my Jump?
game_state: Character with 5 ranks in Tumble making a Jump check.
correct_ruling: Yes. 5 or more ranks in Tumble gives a +2 synergy bonus on Jump checks (and 5 ranks in Jump gives +2 on Tumble).
common_wrong_rulings: No synergy between Tumble and Jump

player_action: I've never trained Open Lock, but I'll just roll Dex and try.
game_state: Fighter with 0 ranks in Open Lock.
correct_ruling: Not allowed. Open Lock is a trained-only skill; a character with no ranks can't attempt it.

player_action: I've got no ranks in Knowledge (arcana), but I want to identify this demon. My Int is 18.
game_state: Identifying the creature is DC 10 + its HD = DC 17.
correct_ruling: Knowledge checks untrained can only answer really easy questions (DC 10 or lower). DC 17 can't be attempted untrained, so the character doesn't know.
common_wrong_rulings: Knowledge is entirely trained-only with no exception

player_action: I tumble past the orc to get behind it. I'll move my full speed.
game_state: Rogue with ranks in Tumble, speed 30 ft, moving through an orc's threatened squares (not through its square).
correct_ruling: Tumbling through threatened squares without provoking requires a DC 15 Tumble check and you move at half speed. Moving at full speed while tumbling is possible only at -10 on the check.
common_wrong_rulings: DC 25 to pass a threatened area (that's through an enemy's square)
Tumble at full speed with no penalty

player_action: I tumble right through the orc's square.
game_state: Rogue with ranks in Tumble; orc is a Medium enemy.
correct_ruling: Moving through an enemy's square with Tumble requires a DC 25 check (at half speed). On failure you stop in the square before the enemy and provoke as normal.

player_action: I'm 4th level. Can I put 8 ranks in Hide? It's a class skill.
game_state: 4th-level rogue.
correct_ruling: No. Max ranks in a class skill is character level + 3 = 7 at 4th level. Cross-class maximum is half that (3.5).

player_action: I'm walking across the narrow ledge. The goblin archer shoots me — am I flat-footed?
game_state: Character with 2 ranks in Balance on a narrow surface.
correct_ruling: Yes. While balancing you're considered flat-footed (lose Dex bonus to AC) unless you have 5 or more ranks in Balance.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 SkillsI.rtf > Balance > Being Attacked while Balancing
common_wrong_rulings: Balancing grants a -2 AC penalty only

player_action: The guard is staring right at me. I hide behind nothing — I'm just really sneaky.
game_state: Open room, no cover or concealment, guard observing the PC.
correct_ruling: Not possible. You can't hide while being observed unless you create a diversion with Bluff (or have an ability like hide in plain sight); in an open room with no cover or concealment there is nowhere to hide.
common_wrong_rulings: Allowing an opposed Hide vs Spot anywhere
confidence_note: The explicit 'need cover or concealment to Hide' wording may be later FAQ text; ruling leans on the SRD's 'can't hide while observed'.

player_action: I shoot from my hiding spot and then hide again immediately (sniping).
game_state: Ranger hidden 20 ft from targets.
correct_ruling: Sniping: if already hidden at least 10 ft away, you can make one ranged attack and then immediately Hide again as a move action, at a -20 penalty on the Hide check.

player_action: I'm a fighter with a 25 Search. I search for the trap: the DC is 28.
game_state: Fighter (no trapfinding), magic trap with Search DC 28.
correct_ruling: Only characters with trapfinding (rogues) can use Search to find traps with a DC higher than 20, so the fighter cannot find it regardless of the roll.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 ClassesI.rtf > Rogue > Trapfinding; SkillsII.rtf > Search
common_wrong_rulings: Anyone can find any trap with a high enough roll

player_action: I make a long jump across a 12-foot chasm with a running start.
game_state: Running start of 20 ft available.
correct_ruling: A running long jump's DC equals the distance in feet: DC 12. Without a 20-ft running start the DC is doubled.

player_action: My climb check failed by 6. I just try again next round, right?
game_state: Character halfway up a wall, Climb DC 15, rolled total 9.
correct_ruling: Failing a Climb check by 4 or less means no progress; failing by 5 or more means the character falls from the height already reached.

player_action: I feint the bugbear so my next attack ignores its Dex.
game_state: Rogue in melee with a bugbear. Rogue lacks Improved Feint.
correct_ruling: Feinting is a standard action: Bluff opposed by the target's Sense Motive (target adds base attack bonus). On success the target is denied its Dex bonus against your next melee attack, which must be made on or before your next turn.
common_wrong_rulings: Feint is a move action without Improved Feint

player_action: I stabilize the dying cleric with the Heal skill.
game_state: Cleric at -4 hp, dying.
correct_ruling: First aid to stabilize a dying character is a standard action requiring a DC 15 Heal check.
